title: Approvals viewer-block descriptions: name can_override_approve (follow-up to #34755)
body:
security#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

Follow-up owed by #34755 (contract review N1, plus two nits). This is text only; behaviour already reads the served predicate.

**Context.** After #34755 the approval request's served `viewer` block carries `can_override_approve` beside `can_override`. The Approve action reads the new flag; Reject, Reassign and Recall keep reading `can_override`.

**Correct these descriptions.** Each still names three viewer leaves, or still ties Approve to `can_override`:

1. The `attachedOnRead` docblock in `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`.
2. The comment over the approvals entry in `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/account.app.ts`.
3. The docblock in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/approvalOverride.ts`.
4. The verify text of the approvals entries in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json`.

**Also:**

5. `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md`: the `onEmptyApprovers` row says `admin_rescue` means "only a privileged admin can act via Reassign". The runtime opens such a request on the organization's administrators. Align the text with `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`.
6. (nit) `approval-override-audit.test.ts`: the letter-case case replaces `engine.find` on the shared double without restoring it. Restore it in the case body, or rebuild the double per case.
7. (nit) If a MySQL or other case-folding test lane exists, add one pin there for the email-target letter-case rule.

**Done when:** each text states the four-leaf viewer block, and Approve reading `can_override_approve`, as served. No behaviour change.
